test_title: PYST 7: SSC MTS 2022 - General Knowledge (Held On: 04 May 2023 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022 aims to regulate mergers and acquisitions based on the value of transactions, and says that deals with transaction value of more than Rs. 2,000 crore will require the Competition Commission of India's approval, For faster approvals, the proposed las also says the timeline for CCI to pass an order on such transactions will be reduced to _______ days from 210 days.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**150**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Recently, the Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022, which seeks to amend the Competition Act, 2002, was passed in the Lower House amid protests from the Opposition.
 
• And the Forest (Conservation) Amendment Bill, 2023 is also introduced in parliament.
 
• For faster approvals, the proposed las also says the timeline for CCI to pass an order on such transactions will be reduced to 150 days from 210 days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Competition Act of 2002** was established to oversee and maintain competition within the Indian marketplace, and it explicitly forbids anti-competitive conduct such as cartels, misuse of a dominant market position, and mergers and acquisitions that might negatively impact competition. 
 
• This Act was later modified by the **Competition (Amendment) Act of 2007.**
 
• The duty of implementing and enforcing the Act falls under the purview of the **Competition Commission of India (CCI).**
 
• The Competition Appellate Tribunal, a legal body formed under the auspices of the **Competition Act of 2002,** is authorized to review and adjudicate on appeals against any decisions, rules, or orders issued by the **CCI.**
 
• However, in **2017, the government replaced the Competition Appellate Tribunal with the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), which now carries out the functions previously performed by the former.****​**
